KBR’s Estates Intelligence is a leading force in public sector Assurance, providing cutting-edge technical platforms and professional services. We support central government and specialist departments in effectively managing delivery, to achieve their strategic goals.
Estates Intelligence offers a compelling market proposition, delivering expertise and solutions to optimise data and information, supporting clients to achieve their objectives. Using our VIAverse platform, our people, processes, knowledge and technology, we integrate validated data and cutting-edge technology to streamline operations, maximise efficiency and value for money.
About the Role
The Strategic Asset Intelligence Manager is a senior role within the Insights and Advisory function, providing strategic asset management leadership and estate intelligence to the client. Working in partnership with the Business Intelligence Manager, the role translates asset information, performance data and lifecycle evidence into proactive, evidence-led recommendations that support Asset Management Plans, FMRs, compliance, risk management and investment prioritisation.
The role is accountable for ensuring that asset information, lifecycle intelligence and estate performance insight are accurate, assured and aligned to operational delivery, contractual outcomes and strategic estate planning. It will help the client move from reactive reporting to proactive decision-making by using condition, performance, risk, compliance and cost data to inform interventions, lifecycle planning and future investment.
Operating as a strategic interface between operations, assurance and the client, the role ensures that estate intelligence not only supports service delivery but also informs long-term estate strategy, optimisation and AI-enabled investment decision support as live performance data matures across the contract.

Complement the Senior Operations Manager by informing operational performance and service optimisation.

Shape the use of live performance data, predictive analytics and AI-enabled decision support to inform investment planning and asset interventions.

Own the integrity and translation of asset data into assured, audit-ready intelligence.
Ensure traceability between asset records, maintenance activity, compliance outcomes and contractual performance.

Maintain confidence that asset-related contractual obligations are being demonstrably delivered.
Mobilisation & Transition to BAU
Lead establishment of asset intelligence capability during mobilisation, aligned to CRAD and mobilisation requirements.
Ensure asset data, structures and systems are configured to support reporting, assurance and decision-making from contract commencement.
Support mobilisation evidence development and readiness assurance activities.
Maintain continuity of asset intelligence through transition into steady-state delivery.
Lifecycle & Performance Insight
Oversee development of lifecycle intelligence supporting asset condition, performance and investment planning.
Provide insight into asset reliability, risk and performance trends to support operational and strategic decisions.
Enable optimisation of maintenance strategies and asset interventions through data-led analysis.
Supporting Delivery & Assurance
Provide asset insight to support operational teams in improving service delivery performance.
Provide asset-related data and evidence to support governance, audit and risk management activities.
Act as subject matter expert for estate and asset intelligence across KBR, client and supply chain partners.
Continuous Improvement & Innovation
Identify opportunities to enhance asset intelligence, reporting and analytical capability.
Support implementation of digital tools, automation and innovation aligned to Estates Intelligence capability.
Drive continuous improvement aligned to contractual obligations and client outcomes.

Experience working with assurance frameworks, audit environments and evidence management.

Who We Are
At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses.  We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive.
The Role
As an AI Innovation Lab Experience Specialist, you will bridge interaction design, engineering, and research to transform client opportunity briefs into tangible, working prototypes and evidence-backed human-AI experiences. Operating under the engagement direction of the Associate Director and Director, you turn ambiguity into momentum—taking customer concepts from brief to service blueprint, agent concept, coded interface, and physical or voice touchpoints.
You build the complete interaction rather than just static screens, defining agent state, confidence levels, permissions, explanations, escalations, and outcomes across digital, spatial, and physical surfaces. Working directly with customers—and leading day-to-day client relationships on smaller engagements—you combine deep craftsmanship in your primary discipline with the range to work across code, design, data, devices, and fabrication to help clients experience and evaluate future technology investments today.
What You Will Do
• Turn briefs into buildable blueprints: Map human-agent-system models, user workflows, knowledge requirements, decision matrices, handoffs, and policy constraints while defining what should remain human-controlled.
• Prototype at the lowest useful fidelity: Move rapidly from sketches and Wizard-of-Oz simulations to coded interfaces, live agents, connected devices, or fabricated physical forms based on the learning objective.
• Make prototypes behave for real: Wire synthetic or real-world data, APIs, LLM/agent frameworks, and external tools to ensure end-to-end credibility rather than static screen flows.
• Conduct research and evaluation: Lead co-design sessions and user testing to diagnose whether friction points stem from the interaction, workflow, policy, underlying data, or AI model.
• Manage customer relationships: Present interactive prototypes, facilitate executive workshops, and act as the primary day-to-day contact on smaller client engagements under Director oversight.
• Capture reusable design patterns: Separate customer-specific details from reusable interaction logic, component libraries, agent states, prompt templates, and evaluation frameworks for broader Lab use.
• Package deliverables for production: Hand off complete flows, code repositories, dependencies, risks, and test evidence to downstream delivery and pilot teams to ensure seamless continuity.
• Explore frontier technologies: Experiment with sensors, microcontrollers, edge devices, and ambient feedback through protected moonshot capacity to advance human-AI collaboration.
Your Future at Kyndryl
Becoming an AI Innovation Lab Experience Specialist at Kyndryl is an excellent gateway to many different paths. You’ll be creating a well-rounded skillset while gaining professional certifications and qualifications. You can evolve horizontally into other technical or non-technical areas, or move vertically into senior leadership or specialized domain roles. There are many different types and flavours of roles at Kyndryl, so everyone can find the opportunity that suits them best.
Who You Are
You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others.
Who You Are
Required Skills and Experience
• Education & Professional Background: Bachelor’s degree in Interaction Design, HCI, Industrial Design, Computer Science, Engineering, Architecture, or equivalent practical experience.
• Experience: 5+ years in creative technology, design technology, interaction design, or software prototyping, with at least 2 years building client-facing prototypes under tight deadlines.
• Portfolio Proof: A portfolio (PDF or link) demonstrating working prototypes you built yourself, highlighting the core questions answered and the resulting design impact.
• Craft Depth & Range: Deep expertise in at least one core making craft (HCI, interaction/product design, industrial design, or software engineering) paired with the versatility to work across code, data, and hardware.
• Practical AI Fluency: Demonstrated ability to build with agentic and generative AI frameworks, integrate APIs/models, and apply AI capabilities responsibly within user workflows.
• Research & Diagnostic Instincts: Experience conducting user testing and co-design sessions, with proven ability to translate evidence into concrete structural improvements.
• Client & Communication Presence: Strong presentation and workshop-facilitation skills, with the professional judgment required to manage client relationships on smaller engagements.
Preferred Skills and Experience
• Advanced Degree & Experience: Master’s degree in Interaction Design, HCI, Design Engineering, or Computational Design, alongside experience in an innovation lab, studio, or agency background.
• Modern Prototyping Tech Stack: Hands-on experience with modern web front ends (TypeScript, React), Figma, Git, API integrations, agent frameworks, and cloud platform tools.
• Embodied, Physical & Spatial AI: Proficiency with microcontrollers/edge devices (Arduino, Raspberry Pi, ESP32), sensors, 3D printing/fabrication, spatial audio, AR/VR (Unity/Unreal), or 3D tools (Blender/Rhino).
• Workplace Mobility: Willingness and flexibility to travel to customer sites and regional Lab locations as engagement needs require.
Being You
The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way.

Job Description:
We are hiring a Carbonate Reservoir Geologist position within our Sedimentology & Stratigraphy (SedStrat) Specialist Team. The team provides deep technical expertise that is applied globally across bp’s Exploration and Reservoir Development portfolio.
This is an individual contributor role that requires a deep understanding of carbonate depositional systems and reservoir architecture, and broad experience of carbonate reservoir production characteristics. The successful candidate must have specifically carbonate sedimentology and reservoir quality expertise with a history of successfully applying and integrating that knowledge in a variety of subsurface projects to create value. In addition, the successful candidate will be able to demonstrate strong project management abilities, as well as excellent communication and influencing skills. This role is suitable for experienced carbonate sedimentologists with a history of business delivery.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Primary accountability would be as one of bp’s recognized carbonate reservoir subject matter experts .
In addition to supporting carbonate-focused projects, the successful candidate must lead subsurface teams across bp to deliver sedimentological and reservoir characterization studies in a range of diverse carbonate settings globally.
• Integrate diverse subsurface static and dynamic data sets working closely with engineers and other subsurface disciplines to identify value-generating opportunities
• Assist in framing and prioritizing technical service work.
• Supervise and verify sedimentological, reservoir quality, and integrated geology studies undertaken in the SedStrat specialist team, and as appropriate, those undertaken in assets.
• Provide input into management presentations and reports.
• Provide carbonate sedimentology and reservoir quality coaching and mentoring in areas of developed expertise across bp.
• Develop and maintain deep carbonate sedimentological and diagenetic skills across a range of reservoir types through reading, attending consortia workshops and external conferences.
• Quickly develop a strong technical reputation as a bp subject matter expert, and where appropriate, publish high quality innovative technical work internally and externally e.g. at industry-wide conferences and formal manuscript publications.
• Assist/lead teaching and development of bp courses with significant carbonate geological content.
• Act as a focal point for carbonate-focused JIPs/consortia, ensuring that maximum value is gained from them.
EDUCATION:
Minimum requirement MSc Geology degree level; preferably PhD level or equivalent experience.
EXPERIENCE AND JOB REQUIREMENTS:
• A deep understanding of carbonate sedimentary rocks across a range of depositional settings (e.g. platform, ramp, reefal, slope, basinal, lacustrine). In particular, the successful candidate will be able to demonstrate a strong understanding of carbonate facies analysis, depositional architecture, diagenesis, reservoir quality evolution, high-resolution sequence stratigraphy, and stratigraphic frameworks.
• An ability to scope and co-ordinate reservoir description and characterization projects, some involving external contractors, to deliver high-quality products that can be practically applied to subsurface problems.
• Experience in carbonate reservoir management/production, and at least one of the following: exploration, appraisal, early field development.
• An ability to describe carbonate core and outcrops independently, to a high standard, integrating sedimentology, textures, diagenesis, fractures, and reservoir quality observations.
• Ability to organize and lead geologic integrated field trips and core workshops, particularly focused on carbonate systems and reservoir analogues.
• Strong communication skills (written and verbal). Experienced with presenting to senior management to influence both vertically and horizontally in the organization.
• Ability to context switch while supporting more than one team at pace with the ability to pragmatically right-scope products.
• Managing carbonate analogues databases and contributing to reservoir quality benchmarking efforts.
AN ABILITY TO:
• Generate multiple depositional, diagenetic, and stratigraphic scenarios
• Use static and dynamic fluid data to test, improve and rank those models
• Describe subsurface uncertainty and risks and their impact on profile and resource delivery
• Skillfully correlate wireline logs, integrate reservoir data (e.g. core, seismic and image logs), dynamic data (sat logs, PLTs, PBU etc) and generate multiple geological models.
• A good understanding of, and ability to integrate with, other subsurface subject areas (Petrophysics, Geophysics, Reservoir Engineering)
DESIRABLE:
• A minimum of 10 years’ broad geological experience, ideally gained through work assignments in different areas and basins, dominantly within carbonate systems.
• Experience working in multi-discipline/multi-function project teams and ability to influence others to provide quality inputs to ensure quality team delivery.
• Ability to organize and lead cross-team workshops and meetings.

Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Coordinator (VSG UK)
The Vesta Software Group acquires, manages, and builds software companies in a variety of vertical markets, enabling them to be clear leaders in their industries. Our companies provide mission-critical enterprise solutions for vertical industries across the entire industry value chain globally.
Being a portfolio group of Jonas Software (within Constellation Software Inc.), the Vesta Software Group is all about strengthening businesses within the markets in which we compete and enabling them to grow – whether through organic measures such as new initiatives and product development, day-to-day business, or through acquisitions.
Job Purpose
The ESG Coordinator will support the development, implementation and ongoing delivery of the Company's Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) strategy. Working closely with Business Unit Leaders, Portfolio Managers, ESG Champions and Senior Leadership Teams globally, the role will coordinate ESG activities, monitor progress against agreed objectives, support ESG reporting and help drive the achievement of the Company's global ESG goals.
Key Responsibilities
• Coordinate and support the rollout of the Company's ESG strategy across all business units.
• Work collaboratively with Business Unit Leaders, Portfolio Managers and the Senior Leadership Team to ensure ESG objectives are embedded within business plans and operational activities, including the completion of the ESG Scorecard on a quarterly basis.
• Coordinate ESG projects and initiatives, ensuring agreed milestones, deadlines and deliverables are achieved.
• Monitor progress against ESG targets and support the collection and analysis of ESG-related data and metrics.
• Identify gaps, inconsistencies and delays in ESG submissions, working with stakeholders to resolve issues and escalating material risks where appropriate.
• Maintain ESG project plans, documentation, action logs and reporting dashboards.
• Support the preparation of ESG reports, updates and presentations for internal stakeholders.
• Coordinate and support ESG Champions across the business with carbon calculation data collection and the use of the Sweep platform.
• Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and support the implementation of new ESG initiatives aligned to the Company's global goals.
• Provide support and training on ESG to new business unit leaders and ESG champions as required.
• Support the collation of information required for ESG reporting and compliance activities, working with internal subject matter experts and external advisers where appropriate.
Knowledge, Skills and Experience
Essential
• Experience coordinating projects and managing multiple workstreams simultaneously.
• Strong organisational and planning skills with excellent attention to detail.
• Ability to analyse information and present findings clearly and accurately.
• Strong Excel skills and confidence working with data and reporting.
• Ability to identify trends, anomalies and gaps within data submissions.
• Ability to manage sensitive and confidential business information appropriately.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across different levels of the organisation.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
Desirable
•
Previous experience working in ESG, sustainability, corporate responsibility or a related field.
• Experience working with sustainability reporting systems or ESG data collection platforms.
• Experience coordinating activities across multiple business units or regions.
• Knowledge of ESG frameworks, reporting standards and emerging sustainability trends.
• Experience producing reports and tracking performance metrics.
Behavioural Competencies
• Collaboration and Teamwork
• Planning and Organisation
• Stakeholder Management
• Continuous Improvement
• Accountability
• Communication
• Attention to Detail
• Proactive Follow-through
Key Relationships
Internal
• Chief People Officer
• ESG Steering Committee
• Senior Leadership Team
• Business Unit Leaders
• Portfolio Managers
• ESG Champions
• Functional teams across the Group
External
• Industry bodies and sustainability partners
• ESG consultants and advisers (where applicable)

More About Jonas Software:
Jonas Software is a leading provider of enterprise management software solutions, serving a wide range of vertical markets including hospitality, healthcare, construction, education, personal care, fitness, leisure, moving and legal services, to name a few. Within these markets, Jonas is comprised of over 65 distinct brands, each a respected leader in its domain.
Jonas’ vision is to be the branded global leader across these verticals and to be recognized by customers and industry stakeholders as the trusted provider of “Software for Life.” We are committed to technology, product innovation, quality, and exceptional customer service.
Jonas Software supports over 60,000 customers in more than 30 countries. We employ over 6,000 skilled professionals, including industry experts and technology specialists. Across our broader network, we support a global workforce of more than 30,000 employees.
Headquartered in Canada, Jonas Software has a global footprint with offices around the world. We’re a 100% owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., based in Toronto, publicly listed on the TSX (CSU.TO), and a member of the S&P/TSX 60 Index.

Hemel Hempstead (Hybrid – 3 days/week in office)
Annual salary + bonus and benefits
Are you a creative strategist who loves turning data into great ideas? We're looking for a Performance Creative Strategist to join our new Marketing Operations team and shape how Haven scales our paid digital creative. You'll drive the testing, the thinking, and the learning – working across channels including Meta, Google, TikTok, and beyond to build paid creative that enables us to quickly scale effective ideas and retire underperforming ones. If you're commercially minded, curious about what works, and ready to bridge the gap between creative excellence and performance results, let's talk.

-        Testing and strategy – Driving testing for paid creative across Meta, Google, TikTok, and other platforms, developing structured hypotheses around messaging, format, visuals, and audience relevance
-        Creative briefing and Production – Working closely with internal and external teams to translate ideas into practical, scalable assets. Define workflows and prompts for AI tools to ensure reliable outputs
-        Performance analysis - Reviewing paid creative performance regularly, analysing results to identify what's working and what isn't, then building a test-and-learn rhythm rather than reactive changes
-        Learning and scaling - Identifying winning creative patterns and scaling them faster, retiring underperforming work quickly, and capturing learnings so they're reused rather than rediscovered
What we’d like you to bring:
-        Performance creative strategy - Strong experience in performance creative strategy, paid social creative, growth creative, or performance marketing environments, with a solid understanding of paid creative across Meta, Google, TikTok, and other auction-based channels
-        Creative hypothesis and testing - Proven ability to develop creative hypotheses, testing plans, and structured learning agendas, with a test-and-learn mindset rather than reactive approaches
-        Data interpretation - Ability to interpret performance data and turn insights into better creative direction, identifying what's working, what isn't, and what should change next
-        Briefing and communication - Strong briefing and communication skills, with confidence articulating creative rationale and working across media, brand, design, and production teams
-        AI and automation - Experience working with AI tools and in highly automated environments, plus familiarity with high-volume consumer sectors (travel, hospitality, leisure, retail) would be valuable

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong.  Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.
Facilities Manager
Objective of Role
The Facilities Manager (FM) will be directly responsible for the provision of facilities services to occupiers in one or more managed properties to best practice standards defined by JLL and is expected to understand the business objectives of the investment.
Team Structure
Reporting to the Senior Facilities Managers (SFM), the FM may have line management responsibilities for Assistant Facilities Manager(s) (AFM) in the region and will work closely in a number of ‘virtual teams’ within PAM including; Client Relationship Directors (CRDs), Contract Directors (CDs), Management Services, Client Financial Services (CFS) and will take direction from Client FM Leads.
Key Responsibilities and Deliverables
Facilities (property/portfolio) Management;
• Working closely and taking direction from relevant Client FM Leads take ownership and be responsible for delivering operational facilities related client KPIs as identified in the PMA (Property Management Agreement) and/or any other client agreed initiatives.
• To assist in the delivery of ‘Instinct’ (customer experience) operational initiatives across your portfolio in close liaison with our service partners.
• To regularly liaise with occupiers and be the principal point of contact for advice and guidance in connection with the day-to-day physical operation of the building.
• Inform Surveyors of any occupier matters that may influence valuation/investment considerations including assistance in monitoring Tenant’s compliance with covenants.
• Report to Surveyors in accordance with an agreed procedure, ensuring the Client or Business Space Lead FM is kept informed on matters relating to standards of facilities management.
• To work in accordance with established procedures in connection with JLLs out of hours cover and emergencies.
• To deliver the financial management of the property through the preparation of service charge budgets, the monitoring of agreed budgets to pre-defined cash limits, quarterly variance reporting and service charge reconciliation to agreed accounting practices. Also, to administer non-recoverable budgets.
• To understand the principal terms of occupier’s leases as they affect the facilities management of the property and the Client’s obligations to provide services including clarity on the extent of the common areas.
• In conjunction with the Surveyors and RFM, ensure that the procurement of all supplies and services at the property is undertaken in accordance with the JLLs PAM procurement program to ensure the highest standards for the best price. This will include the use of accredited Contractors only, usually on the basis of framework agreements, and JLLs purchase ordering systems.
• Monitor contractor performance against agreed standards. Review service contracts as appropriate.
• Establish and maintain high quality health and safety arrangements, in accordance with best practice guidelines from central support under the JLLs risk management programme and the RFM.
• To ensure all risks identified in the independent Risk Assessment are properly addressed and to review risks as part of JLLs audit process and Site Compliance inspections.
• To work with other aspects of JLLs ‘Socially Responsible Management’ programme in relation to environmental & sustainability policies; to include water hygiene and asbestos monitoring etc.
• To ensure reactive maintenance and day-to-day service requirements undertaken in a timely and cost-effective manner.
• This job description sets out key elements and responsibilities of the role, but it is not intended to be exhaustive and does not constitute a contractual document. Duties may be changed to meet changing needs or circumstances.
• Be familiar with all heating, ventilating, mechanical and electrical equipment in each building and have a sound understanding of the purpose and general working of such equipment. To ensure maintenance contracts in place to cover O&M manual requirements.
• Assist and liaise with building surveyors/architects/consultants on major works.
• With the Surveyors, identify and arrange minor planned works.
• To maintain, test and implement disaster planning procedures to cover all emergencies. To organise and co-ordinate fire evacuation and bomb drills.
• Prepare site regulations and issue permits to work for all contractor activities on site.
• To ensure that on-site management of the properties is undertaken in accordance with JLLs polices, processes and procedures as defined on the PAM Process Hub site (Connect).
• Establish and maintain proper site records in accordance with best practice rules.
• Responsible for routine correspondence using standard documents and templates as appropriate.
• Develop and maintain occupier handbooks as per defined standard for each site.
• To monitor vacant/void property in conjunction with the clients’ insurance policy.
• Establish a regular inspection programme for each site in accordance with site insurance and regulatory requirements.
• Assist in the submission of insurance claims relating to incidents on site and manage the obtaining of quotes and/or works at site as instructed by the insurers or loss adjusters.
• Ensure readiness for sale of relevant individual properties dealing with due diligence enquiries on disposal and lettings from a facilities perspective.
Required Qualifications, Skills and Experience
• Commercial awareness and ability to develop identified business improvement opportunities
• Solid stakeholder management skills and an ability to understand and relay business ideas
• Previous experience working for a company within the property industry or from a similar business line, with client facing experience or from a corporate FM background
• An advocate of change and supportive in driving operational business change
• IWFM / BIFM qualification and or similar in facilities operational management
• Strong organisation skills and excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
• Driven to achieve results
• Knowledge of safety, quality, and cost risks

• A structured learning and development journey.

• We cannot sponsor visas.
• Knowledge of at least one modern programming language or framework.
• A genuine passion for technology and the drive to keep learning.
Locations
Choose from Manchester, Leeds, Watford (London), Cardiff or Chester. With our hybrid working policy, all colleagues spend at least two days a week in the office.

Intapp is building a new Majors organization focused on deepening and expanding our relationships with the world's leading Private Capital and Investment Banking firms. We're looking for an accomplished enterprise seller to personally own and materially grow a select portfolio of our largest and most strategic clients.
This is a ground-floor opportunity to help shape how Intapp approaches its most important accounts while working alongside a senior team focused exclusively on strategic client growth. You'll own the commercial strategy for your clients—building relationships at the highest levels, developing a point of view on where Intapp can create greater business value, identifying significant white-space opportunities, and leading complex enterprise sales opportunities from strategy through close.
You'll be building from a position of strength. Intapp already has deep relationships and credibility across Private Capital and Investment Banking. The opportunity is to take those relationships significantly further as we expand our platform and bring differentiated AI capabilities, including Celeste, to market.
We're looking for someone who has done this before—someone who has personally owned some of their company's largest enterprise relationships, earned credibility in the boardroom, influenced client technology and business strategy, orchestrated their organization around the client, and materially grown those accounts.
What You Will Do
•
Own your accounts. Take direct commercial responsibility for a select portfolio of Intapp's largest Private Capital and Investment Banking relationships, with accountability for expansion, retention, and long-term revenue growth.
•
Build the growth strategy. Develop multi-year strategic account plans that identify white space, executive relationships, competitive exposure, new use cases, and significant opportunities to expand Intapp's footprint.
•
Operate at the executive level. Build trusted relationships with Managing Partners, CEOs, CIOs, CFOs, COOs, and other senior leaders, bringing a point of view that can influence business and technology decisions.
•
Create opportunity—not just respond to it. Proactively uncover client challenges and strategic priorities, connect them to Intapp's capabilities, and create complex enterprise opportunities that may not already exist.
•
Lead the sale. Personally own high-value, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from opportunity creation and business case development through executive alignment, negotiation, and close.
•
Orchestrate Intapp around the client. Bring together Product, Client Success, Solutions Consulting, Professional Services, and executive leadership to deliver a unified strategy around each major relationship.
•
Expand the platform relationship. Connect capabilities across DealCloud, Risk & Compliance, Celeste, and the broader Intapp platform to client priorities and measurable business outcomes.
•
Lead the AI conversation. Engage senior executives on how AI is changing Private Capital and Investment Banking, bringing a credible perspective on where agentic AI can transform workflows, productivity, relationship intelligence, and decision-making.
•
Deliver growth. Build and convert a substantial expansion pipeline, maintain rigorous opportunity and forecast discipline, and consistently deliver against ambitious revenue targets.
What You Will Need
•
A demonstrated track record of personally owning and materially growing large, complex enterprise relationships within Private Capital, Investment Banking, financial technology, data, enterprise SaaS, or closely adjacent markets.
•
Experience carrying significant revenue responsibility and consistently creating, developing, and closing complex enterprise expansion opportunities.
•
Deep understanding of Private Capital and/or Investment Banking, including how firms operate, make technology decisions, and evaluate strategic investments.
•
Boardroom-level presence and persuasion—the ability to establish credibility quickly, challenge senior executives constructively, bring a compelling point of view, and influence consequential decisions.
•
Evidence that you can move beyond product selling to understand a client's business, identify where technology can create value, and turn that insight into significant commercial opportunity.
•
Experience navigating complex global organizations, building multi-threaded executive relationships, and creating consensus across numerous stakeholders.
•
The ability to mobilize and lead internal resources without direct authority, bringing the right people together around a clear client strategy.
•
Commercial fluency around AI and its implications for Private Capital and Investment Banking. You don't need to be a technologist, but you should be capable of leading credible conversations with senior executives about how AI can change the way their firms operate.
•
A combination of strategic thinking and sales execution—you can build a three-year vision for an account and still personally drive the opportunity required to deliver this quarter's number.
What you will gain:
At Intapp, you’ll get the opportunity to bring your talents and intellectual curiosity to create better outcomes for our people and our clients. You’ll be part of a growing public company, with a modern work environment that’s connected yet flexible and where your professional growth and well-being are top priorities.
We’ll collaborate and grow together, supporting each other in a positive, open atmosphere that fosters creativity, innovation, and teamwork.
Here, you will have the opportunity to:
•
Expand Your Skills: Unlock your potential with professional development opportunities supported by a community of experienced professionals. We offer reimbursement for training and continuing education to help you stay ahead in your career.
•
Enjoy Where You Work: Thrive in our modern, open offices designed to inspire creativity and collaboration. Our complimentary lunches and fully stocked kitchens ensure you have everything you need to stay energized throughout the day.
•
Support What Matters Most: Our comprehensive wellness and flexible time off programs and our benefits are designed to care for you and your family. Our family-formation benefits and support during your family-building journey ensure you have the resources you need when it matters most. We believe in giving back and supporting our communities with paid volunteer time off and a donation matching program for the causes you care about.
Join us and be a part of a collaborative and welcoming culture where your contributions are valued, and your professional growth is a priority. Together, we are building a company of long-term value that we can all be proud of.

Are you an experienced Systems Safety Engineer or Safety Manager looking for your next challenge in Defence? We are looking for a safety engineering leader who combines sound technical judgement with the experience to develop people, influence engineering decisions and help shape how safety is delivered across complex Maritime systems. If you understand that product safety starts with good engineering and are motivated to challenge established approaches and improve how things are done, we would like to hear from you.
Salary: Circa £70,000 depending on experience
Dynamic (hybrid) working: 2-3 days per week onsite due to workload classification
Security Clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.
What we can offer you:
• Company Bonus: Bonus of up to 21% of base salary
• Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
• Flexible working: We welcome applicants who are looking for flexible working arrangements
• Enhanced parental leave: offers up to 26 weeks for maternity, adoption and shared parental leave -enhancements are available for paternity leave, neonatal leave and fertility testing and treatments
• Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
• Healthcare Cash Plan: The Healthcare Cash Plan benefit provides the option to claim cash back on everyday healthcare expenses such as optical, dental, health and wellbeing and more.
The opportunity:
Join our Safety and Reliability Engineering Department as a Maritime Safety Group Lead, leading a team of safety engineers supporting complex Maritime Defence programmes.
This is a role for someone who can bring together technical expertise, people leadership and a broader perspective on the future of safety engineering. You will build on the strengths of the existing team, bringing complementary experience and fresh thinking to help us meet changing engineering demands.
As product development accelerates and digital technologies transform the engineering environment, safety engineering must adapt too. You will help the team respond to these changes, improve how we work and ensure that safety remains integral to product design and development.
The Role
You will lead and develop a team of safety engineers while retaining a hands-on technical contribution. Working closely with design teams, systems engineers and other stakeholders, you will apply safety engineering techniques to understand hazards, assess risk and influence the design of complex products.
You will prepare and guide the development of hazard analyses, safety cases and supporting technical evidence, applying engineering judgement to determine what is needed to demonstrate that risks have been adequately addressed. You will also help integrate safety engineering into the wider systems engineering process, ensuring that safety informs design decisions rather than becoming an activity focused solely on compliance or documentation.
Alongside delivering across multiple projects, you will support the development of your team, encourage constructive challenge and identify opportunities to improve our engineering processes and practices. You will need to balance technical priorities, people development and delivery commitments while helping the function adapt to changing ways of working.
What are we looking for?
• Experienced safety engineer: A strong background in systems safety engineering, product safety engineering or a related discipline, ideally within Defence or another complex, safety-critical industry.
• Engineering-led approach: Practical experience applying safety engineering techniques to equipment and systems design, working with design teams to identify hazards, understand failure mechanisms and influence risk-reduction measures.
• Leadership capability: Experience leading or developing engineers, coordinating workloads and supporting effective delivery across multiple projects.
• Technical breadth: Knowledge of hazard analysis, functional failure analysis, fault tree analysis, safety cases and supporting evidence.
• Systems engineering knowledge: An understanding of how safety engineering integrates with system development and product certification, including relevant UK and international standards such as Defence Standard 00-056.
• Constructive challenge: The confidence to question established approaches, bring complementary expertise and work collaboratively with colleagues to reach sound engineering decisions.
• Adaptability: An interest in continuous improvement and the ability to respond to rapid development, digital transformation and the effective use of digital technologies in engineering.
• Communication and judgement: Strong analytical, interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and balance technical risk with programme priorities.
• Developing others: A commitment to sharing knowledge, mentoring engineers and building a capable, collaborative team.
• Qualifications: A relevant engineering degree or equivalent professional experience.
Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given
MBDA is a leading defence organisation.  We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom.
We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity, Disability and more…

Your Impact
​We are looking for a Principal RF Engineer to join Leonardo in Edinburgh. Leonardo are a world-class defence Technology Company. We develop cutting-edge Radars as well as Maritime and Airborne surveillance systems. We are also investors in innovation, undertaking all our own research to fuel our future products. This role sits within the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) Multifunction RF System (MRFS) team, where you will join our growing Electronics team to contribute to the delivery of a key Technology Demonstrator Programme (TDP), paving the way for the next generation of fire control radar.
Hybrid working - in this role it is possible to work from home some of the time, but the nature of the work and security requirements mean that you should expect to be mostly working on site.
What You’ll Do as a Principal RF Engineer
This is an exciting opportunity for you as an engineer to bring your skillset and knowledge into our working environment. You will be involved in developing a range of multifunctional RF, PCB and Module designs using the latest technologies available and contribute to the definition and execution of a testing and integration phase of a key TDP to enable GCAP.
As an RF/Microwave engineer, you will be responsible for:
• Full hardware lifecycle for our products: from system concept, through detailed design and prototyping, test and verification, system integration and support in production.
• Creating high quality and robust designs, conducting design reviews for your design, fully documenting and recording your work products, keeping them under configuration management and providing plans and progress reports.
• Developing a range of multifunctional RF PCB and Module designs using the latest technologies available and enhancing your understanding of key design and manufacture processes.
• Designing to test, creating test prototypes for design validation, verification of development models and support for production test.
• Preparing robust manufacturing data packs and provide technical support to sub-contracts and engineering interface with manufacturing.
• Working closely with Systems, Test and Electronics engineers, you will be solving real integration problems on advanced systems
• Coach and mentor junior team members to support the development of a high-performance engineering team in preparation for the delivery of the demands of the GCAP programme
What you’ll bring
You will ideally have experience in a number of the following areas:
• RF microwave sub-system design
• RF system test and integration
• Lab measurements such as signal generation, spectrum analysis and vector network analysis
• Microwave design tools
• GaAs/GaN MMIC design and application
• Design of passive microwave structures
• Low phase noise design and measurement
• Microwave component selection
• Technical report writing
• Design reviews and lifecycle management
This role requires you to have:
• Degree qualified in Electrical & Electronic Engineering (preferable) or related science (e.g. Physics).
• Proven experience (5+ years) in RF circuit design and analysis and a strong understanding of microwave techniques and electromagnetic theory
• Ability to work effectively and lead in a collaborative team environment
Personal attributes and values are just as important to us as technical ability so we are looking for engineers with a willingness to learn, progress and develop through our devoted technical career path. If you are passionate in what you do and can deliver a pragmatic approach to problem-solving we would like to hear from you.
Security Clearance
Please note that to apply for this opportunity you must be eligible for UK security clearance. Normally this is to the level of Security Check (typically known as “SC”) for our business which includes having a minimum of 5 years permanent residency in the UK. For more information and guidance please visit:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.

• Rewarding Performance: All employees at management level and below are eligible for our bonus scheme.
• Never Stop Learning: Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn Learning.
• Refer a friend: Receive a financial reward through our referral programme.
• Tailored Perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.
• Flexible working: Flexible hours with hybrid working options. For part time opportunities, please talk to us about what might be possible for this role.

jll.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/jllcareers/job.description_excerpt:
JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way.
Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong.  Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.
JLL | Work Dynamics Consulting | London
Our clients’ challenges are increasingly complex, dynamic and wide-ranging. Consultants are at the forefront of helping clients navigate this complexity and find practical solutions that drive impact and value. Our consulting team is one of the biggest in the market, we work with colleagues across JLL and are powered by JLL’s own data and technology. We work with some of the world’s largest and most interesting companies across all sectors and geographies.
We’re growing, and we’re looking for an Associate Director and a Director to join our UK Consulting practice.
What you'll be doing
No two projects are the same. You’ll work in highly skilled, cross-functional teams that will stretch you and reward you. Recent projects include:
• Leading a client's real estate transformation end to end: strategic programme oversight, programme management, FM project management, business and real estate strategies, change management, and pulling in and directing other JLL service lines
• Developing business cases and working with JLL Technology to build proof-of-concept AI agents that streamline client real estate workflows and cut out inefficiency
• Designing new target operating models for clients navigating organisational complexity and then embedding the change alongside them
• Leading the real estate divestment for a client separating part of their business or acquiring a business: untangling the property portfolio, contracts and obligations tied to the part being divested or streamlined, while the rest of the estate keeps running.
What the role looks like at each level:
Associate Director - you'll lead delivery on individual engagements and workstreams, start building your own client relationships, and take a growing role in proposals and pitches. You're client-facing, comfortable owning a workstream from start to finish, and ready to shape business development rather than just supporting it.
Director - you'll own client relationships at a senior level, lead multi-workstream programmes, and help grow the practice: shaping the proposition, winning new work and building the team around you. You'll be a visible presence with clients and across JLL.
Is this you?
• You've done hands-on consulting work in corporate real estate: target operating model (TOM) design, FM strategy, location strategy, portfolio strategy, PMO, AI adoption, change management or something close to it?
• You'd rather see your recommendations actually happen, even if you're not the one delivering every step?
• You're comfortable when a problem doesn't arrive pre-labelled. When a client is struggling with the pace of change hitting their business, that's exactly the kind of ambiguity you thrive on.
• Above all, you're the person clients want in the room when things get messy. Not because you have all the answers, but because you'll help them find the way forward.
If you're going for Director: you've built and grown client relationships yourself, not just delivered against ones others have won. You know the difference between being liked by a client and being trusted by one, and you've been on the right side of that line more often than not.
What you'll get
A team that's building something right now, not maintaining a legacy practice. Exposure to some of the biggest occupiers and brands. A voice in how the consulting proposition evolves, rather than a fixed script to deliver against. Colleagues who'll tell you the truth about a deliverable before the client does. And because JLL delivers as well as advises, you’ll see your strategy put into practice across the wider business.
Location:
On-site –London, GBR

The Corporate Engineering AI team is the central enablement and platform delivery function for LSEG’s internal agentic AI ecosystem. The team’s mission is to scale safe, high‑quality AI capabilities across the enterprise by providing shared platforms, patterns, governance, and delivery support.
CE AI owns and operates core AI platforms including LSEG AI Assist, the Question Answering Service (QAS), and the Internal MCP Gateway. Rather than delivering individual business use cases end‑to‑end, the team enables product engineering groups across LSEG to expose knowledge, data, and actions to AI agents in a consistent, governed, and repeatable way.
The team operates a Central MCP Delivery model: building critical MCP tools and services “for” product teams where required, while simultaneously defining standards, patterns, and platform capabilities that allow teams to progressively move towards self‑service contribution.
LSEG AI Assist / Internal MCP Programme of Work
This programme delivers an LSEG‑owned, production‑grade agentic AI platform with MCP as its extensibility layer.

*   Building and operating LSEG AI Assist, an in‑house agentic experience capable of reasoning, planning, and tool‑calling.

*   Delivering a production Internal MCP Gateway providing discovery, security, policy enforcement, observability, and lifecycle management for MCP tools and Skills.
*   Designing and building MCP servers and Skills that expose internal and vendor systems safely to agents.
*   Establishing evaluation, quality control, and governance mechanisms so MCP tools and Skills can be promoted through PTB/PTO and operated with confidence at scale.
The programme follows a “build for” model today, with a strong emphasis on defining the future product and platform experience, patterns, and contribution pathways that will enable federated scale over time.
ML Engineers – Responsibilities & Skills

*   Build secure API wrappers where backend systems lack suitable authentication or entitlement models.
*   Work closely with product teams in a “build for” capacity, transferring knowledge and establishing reusable patterns.
*   Shape the developer experience for MCP and Skills, including templates, contribution guidance, and standards.
*   Collaborate with Quality Engineers and SREs to ensure solutions meet quality, governance, and operational readiness expectations.
Skills
*   Strong Python development experience.
*   Hands‑on experience with LLM and agent frameworks and agentic reasoning patterns.
*   Practical understanding of Model Context Protocol (MCP), including server and tool patterns.
*   FastAPI and REST API design and implementation experience.
*   Experience with prompt engineering and RAG‑based architectures.
*   Containerisation and Kubernetes‑based deployment experience.
*   Ability to work across platform, product, and governance boundaries in an enterprise environment.

Job Description: Equipment Engineer Wafer Fab and Epitaxy (Continental Shift)
Location: Caswell, Northamptonshire
Reports to: Equipment Engineering Shift Manager
About Lumentum
Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) is a global leader in innovative optical and photonic products enabling optical networking and commercial laser customers worldwide. Our technologies are integral to virtually every type of telecom, enterprise, and data centre network, and support advanced manufacturing and next generation sensing applications. Lumentum’s UK wafer fabrication facility in Caswell is a centre of excellence for high-performance optoelectronic devices used in telecommunications and industrial systems.
Role Summary
As an Equipment Technician, you will provide technical support for the operation and maintenance of wafer fabrication and epitaxy equipment on a continental shift pattern. This role offers the opportunity to work on advanced III-V semiconductor technologies within a highly specialised UK fabrication facility, supporting products deployed globally in next-generation communications networks. Your primary focus will be the fault diagnosis, repair, and optimisation of advanced semiconductor process tools including vacuum, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, and RF systems, as well as equipment handling hazardous process gases and chemicals.
This is a hands-on, high-precision engineering role ideal for those with experience maintaining complex electro-mechanical systems in critical environments including high-tech manufacturing, aerospace, defence, or UK Armed Forces technical trades.
Key Responsibilities
• Provide rapid first-line engineering response to minimise tool downtime and production impact.
• Conduct repairs, fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance on semiconductor processing equipment including, but not limited to lithography, etch, PVD, PECVD and MOVPE reactor systems.
• Manage chemical and specialty gas supply systems in compliance with statutory, site safety and environmental standards.
• Support maintenance of gas delivery, exhaust and abatement systems associated with epitaxy and PECVD tools.
• Manage spare parts inventory to ensure availability of critical components and minimise downtime.
• Implement and support preventative maintenance strategies to maximise OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) and uptime.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives (Kaizen, 6S, 8D) and maintain accurate documentation of actions and outcomes.
• Participate in production and planning meetings to represent equipment engineering performance.
• Support the site emergency response function including participation in the Site Emergency Response Team.
• Fork-lift truck operation will be required (training will be provided).
Key Relationships
• Process and Equipment Engineering Teams
• Facilities and Maintenance Teams
• Manufacturing Operations Team
• MES (PROMIS) and IT Teams
Qualifications
Apprenticeship, HNC, HND or Degree in an Electrical or Mechanical Engineering discipline (or equivalent). Alternatively, a minimum of 5 years’ directly relevant experience in complex electro-mechanical system maintenance.
Preferred Backgrounds and Transferable Skills
We actively welcome applications from engineers with experience in high-reliability environments such as aerospace, defence, automotive manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, oil & gas, power generation, or UK Armed Forces technical trades. Direct semiconductor experience is advantageous but not essential.
Skills
Essential:
• Proven experience in a high-tech, precision-engineering environment.
• Strong fault-finding and diagnostic ability across electrical, electronic and mechanical systems.
• Ability to work safely with hazardous gases and chemicals.
• Ability to follow detailed documented procedures with minimal supervision.
• Competence in documenting procedures, risk assessments, and method statements.
• Effective time management and organisational skills.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
• Team-oriented approach with excellent communication skills.
• Ability to read and interpret technical documentation and communicate effectively within a safety-critical manufacturing environment.
Desirable:
• Previous experience within a semiconductor or cleanroom manufacturing environment.
Other Requirements
• 40.3 hours per week on a continental shift pattern (2 days, 2 nights, 4 off), 12-hour shifts including weekends and bank holidays as part of the continental rotation.
• Work is performed within a cleanroom environment (cleanroom garments provided).
• Role requires use of Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA). Candidates must be able to meet the medical and respiratory protective equipment (RPE) face-fit requirements associated with SCBA use in accordance with site safety standards.
• Must be eligible to work in the UK.
• The Caswell site is located in a rural setting in Northamptonshire. A full UK driving licence and access to own transport are essential.
Equal Opportunities
Lumentum is committed to equal opportunities and actively seeks applications from all sections of the community regardless of sex, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, dependents, age, religion, or belief.
We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.

This is a coaching and upskilling role with genuine technical depth. You need to know how production AI systems work so you can credibly train others to build, test, document, and govern their own.
You will work across OBG’s Technology function, driving adoption of our internal AI platform (KAIT) from early - adopter usage into mainstream, habitual practice. That means running workshops where people leave having built working solutions themselves, coaching product and engineering teams through scoping and delivering their own AI.
use cases, and ensuring that security, data governance, and release processes are embedded from the very first conversation — not bolted on at the end.
Today, roughly 20% of employees generate 80% of AI platform activity. Your job is to close that gap within Tech — upskilling teams so they move from occasional use to confident, governed, daily AI-assisted working. Where you spot gaps in process, documentation, or governance, you flag them and work with the relevant owners to close them.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Coaching & Upskilling
• Design and deliver hands-on technical workshops for Tech teams — the kind where participants build and ship working AI agents themselves, not watch someone else do it.
• Coach engineers and domain experts through identifying real use cases in their function, scoping them rigorously, and building their first working solutions on KAIT. Your success is measured by what they can do independently after you’ve worked with them.
• Run structured AI opportunity audits within Tech teams: helping teams assess which use cases are quick wins they can deliver themselves, which need Architect-level guidance, and which are not worth pursuing.
• Create technical training content covering topics such as RAG (connecting AI to internal knowledge bases), AI agent design, prompt engineering, and API integration — written for a Tech audience, grounded in real OBG scenarios.
• Provide floor support during workshop sessions, including live debugging and troubleshooting — guiding participants through solving problems, not solving for them.
Governance, Security & Process
• Ensure security, data governance, and compliance are embedded into every use case from the start — not treated as a gate at the end. Train teams to think about data classification, human oversight, and audit requirements as part of their design process.
• Upskill teams on OBG’s Technology Release Process so they can self-serve: preparing documentation, completing governance checklists, and meeting production standards without needing hand-holding.
• Identify gaps in existing processes, documentation, or governance frameworks and flag them to the relevant owners. Where guidance is missing or unclear, work with A&I and platform teams to close those gaps through training and upskilling.
Use Case Pipeline & Enablement at Scale
• Coach Tech Innovators (domain experts building use cases) through the full lifecycle: from identifying where AI adds genuine value, through scoping and prototyping, to handing off complex builds for Architect-level support where needed.
• For high-complexity use cases (multi-system integrations, MCP connectors, RAG pipelines), guide and upskill the teams responsible for delivery rather than owning the build yourself. Your role is to transfer capability, not accumulate it.
• Assess incoming use cases and route them correctly: straightforward agent builds that teams can own, strategic projects needing deeper technical support, and cases that belong in data science or other disciplines rather than KAIT.
Developer Productivity (Secondary — ~20% of Time)
• Deliver structured workshops and a best-practice guide for coding assistant adoption (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Cursor) across engineering teams. Engineering team leads retain accountability for sustained adoption in their teams.
• This is a secondary workstream. If the main AI enablement pipeline requires full capacity, developer productivity work is deprioritised.
Required Skills & Qualifications
Essential
• 4–7 years in a hands-on technical role — data engineering, AI/ML engineering, solutions architecture, or DevOps — with a subsequent move into enablement, consultancy, or internal transformation.
• Proven experience coaching technical teams to build and deploy AI agents or RAG pipelines in production — not just building them yourself.
• Hands-on with at least one low-code/no-code automation platform (e.g. n8n) — enough to credibly train others.
• Strong prompt engineering knowledge: system-level prompts, structured output, chain-of-thought, evaluation techniques — and the ability to teach these to others.
• Solid understanding of enterprise integration patterns: REST APIs, OAuth/SSO authentication, rate limiting, data flow between systems.
• Demonstrable commitment to governance and process: you embed security, data classification, and compliance into how teams work, and you flag gaps when processes are missing or unclear.
• Track record of delivering technical workshops where participants built tangible solutions themselves — not lecture-based training.
• Ability to translate complex technical concepts clearly for non-technical audiences and present credibly to senior stakeholders.
Highly Desirable
• Experience in a regulated industry: igaming, fintech, or financial services.
• Hands-on n8n experience for production workflow automation.
• Familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or similar frameworks for connecting AI agents to enterprise systems.
• Experience with LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) for inference and evaluation.
• Working knowledge of vector databases, embedding models, and semantic search.
• Experience with coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor) in a developer productivity context.
• Multi-site or international delivery experience.

The Corporate Engineering AI team is the central enablement and platform delivery function for LSEG’s internal agentic AI ecosystem. The team’s mission is to scale safe, high‑quality AI capabilities across the enterprise by providing shared platforms, patterns, governance, and delivery support.
CE AI owns and operates core AI platforms including LSEG AI Assist, the Question Answering Service (QAS), and the Internal MCP Gateway. Rather than delivering individual business use cases end‑to‑end, the team enables product engineering groups across LSEG to expose knowledge, data, and actions to AI agents in a consistent, governed, and repeatable way.

This programme delivers an LSEG‑owned, production‑grade agentic AI platform with MCP as its extensibility layer.

*   Building and operating LSEG AI Assist, an in‑house agentic experience capable of reasoning, planning, and tool‑calling.

Skills

About Halma
Halma is a global group of life‑saving technology companies, driven by our purpose to grow a safer, cleaner, healthier future for everyone, every day. Named as one of Britain's Most Admired Companies, our company provides innovative products and services that help solve many of the health, environmental and safety problems facing the world today.
Our operating companies are autonomous by design. They own their P&Ls, their customers and their decisions, and that closeness to market is the engine of our growth — not a problem to be tidied away. We are looking for an ambitious, curious and humble procurement professional who is energised, rather than frustrated, by that reality.
Halma employs over 9,000 people in more than 50 companies around the world, with major operations in the UK, Europe, USA, and Asia Pacific. Halma is an equal‑opportunity employer, and achieving diversity is a priority for us.
To find out more about our purpose, our people, our DNA and our impact, please visit: www.halma.com.
The Opportunity
We’re looking for a high-impact Procurement Manager who can unlock the collective buying power of a multi-billion-pound, 50-company group without ever taking control away from the companies that make it work.
This is deliberately not a centralisation role. You won’t be mandating processes, rolling out a single system, or pulling spend into the centre. Your job is to make group-scale value so visible, so easy and so commercially compelling that our companies choose to take it — not because they’re told to. You’ll work across a wide range of direct and indirect categories (materials, electronics, IT, services and capital equipment), creating leverage that operating companies opt into, as well as managing Group level, Enterprise wide procurement for Technology.
This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who thrives in a non‑hierarchical, collaborative, and decentralized environment, and is excited by the chance to drive and develop the procurement opportunities across the Halma Group.
How You’ll Work — Our Procurement Philosophy
This role lives or dies on a particular way of operating.
• Lead through influence, evidence and trust — never mandate. Adoption is earned, not enforced.
• Aggregate demand by invitation, not instruction — opt-in frameworks, lead-buyer arrangements and shared deals that companies join because the value is clear.
• Treat complexity as a feature, not a fault. Many ERPs, many processes and many ways of working are the price of autonomy; we create value inside that reality rather than trying to engineer it away.
• Enable, rather than replace. We make local buyers and engineers stronger — we don’t take ownership off them.
Earn the right to the next conversation by delivering the last one.
If your instinct is to consolidate, standardise and drive compliance, this isn’t the role for you. If your instinct is to build coalitions and let great value sell itself, read on.
What You’ll Be Doing
• Group Leverage by Consent: Spot where common spend exists across autonomous companies and build opt-in frameworks, aggregated deals and lead-buyer arrangements that companies voluntarily adopt — capturing scale benefits without central control.
• Category Strategy in Partnership: Co-create category strategies with operating companies, sharing market insight, strengthening supply resilience and respecting local context and constraints.
• Trusted Advisor & Enabler: Coach and equip local teams; share should-cost models, market intelligence and supplier insight that make them better buyers — building communities of practice, not control points.
• Influence Without Authority: Win voluntary buy-in through credibility, data and relationships across businesses that each have their own ways of working.
• Navigate Complexity: Create leverage across fragmented systems, categories and geographies without forcing standardisation — knowing when harmonisation genuinely adds value and when local difference should be protected.
• Innovation, Automation & AI: and propose automation and AI tools (including Copilot) to make sourcing, contracting and supplier management faster and more transparent — and to make participating in group initiatives effortless.
• Contracting & Supplier Value: Lead group-level contract activity that delivers measurable value, strong governance and improved supplier performance — offered as a proposition companies want, not a rule they must follow.
• Market Intelligence: Stay ahead of commodity movements, supply risk and innovation opportunities, sharing insight proactively to inform decisions and build the case for collaboration.
What We’re Looking For:
Top 5 Hard Skills
• Federated leverage — aggregating demand and leveraging volume across autonomous or independent businesses through opt-in frameworks, lead-buyer, consortium or category-council models, without centralising control.
• Strategic sourcing & category management across direct and indirect spend (materials, electronics, IT, services, capital equipment).
• Contracting & supplier performance management (governance, value delivery, risk/compliance) — designed as compelling propositions companies choose to adopt.
• Spend & market analysis / market intelligence — used to persuade, build the commercial case for collaboration, and strengthen supply resilience.
• Digital procurement tools (eProcurement, contract lifecycle management, automation/AI such as Copilot) — especially to make group participation easy, transparent and low-friction.
Top 5 Soft Skills
• Influencing without authority — building coalitions and voluntary adoption in a decentralised, non-hierarchical group.
• Comfort with deliberate complexity and ambiguity — thriving where there is no single process, system or reporting line, and creating value inside that.
• Stakeholder credibility across functions and seniority — from buyers and engineers to MDs and Presidents.
• An enablement mindset — making local teams better buyers rather than taking ownership from them; coaching, sharing and building networks.
• Ownership, curiosity and bias to action — a hands-on “do-er” who will raise a PO and build a strategy, and who keeps finding novel, innovation-led ways to unlock value.
Your Background
• A background in procurement, sourcing, category management or commercial roles — ideally gained in a multi-business, federated, M&A-heavy or otherwise decentralised environment.
• A persuader and coalition-builder, not a controller; someone who creates pull, not push.
• A self-starter who is comfortable with autonomy, ambiguity and complexity.
• A do-er willing to cover the whole range of procurement activity, from raising POs to building group strategy.

Job Description:
The opportunity:
Our Central London team is looking for talented and enthusiastic Industrial Placement Analytics Engineer to help perform weapon system assessments for our UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) customer. The role will suit those with a STEM background who wish to apply their abilities in a technical analysis and systems assessment environment.
The type of project you will be working on:
• Customer Integration: You will be a member of a weapons project team within our larger Defence Analytics Group working in Central London. The group is integrated into a joint unit with government employees, members of the armed forces, and other contractors.
• The Challenge: To conduct analysis to assess the performance and capability of weapon systems. Problems are solved through the application of scientific methods, physical principles, and analytics to complex data sets. This process may involve new techniques and their encapsulation in improved tools.
• Collaboration: You will be working in close liaison with similar teams within the UK and partner nations, with the opportunity to contribute, influence, challenge and improve joint ways of working and knowledge.
• Breadth: You will be working in an environment where both the complexity and capabilities of the systems are continually evolving throughout the world.
What you’ll do:
• Conduct analysis through the application of physical principles to real world problems. This will be facilitated using the suite of in-house software tools and the occasional development of ad-hoc software, primarily in Python.
• Production of reports and presentations of your work and presentation of them to local MOD customers and the wider community both within the UK and partner nations.
• Provide ad hoc advice and support to MOD customers, often at short notice.
• Travel for technical exchanges with our partners, in the UK and potentially abroad.
What we need from you:
• A STEM background with an emphasis on numerical and analytical skills, with the ability to apply these to real world problems.
• A good understanding of scientific methods and their use through the application of fundamental physical principles.
• Good Interpersonal skills to facilitate collaborative and effective working within an inter-disciplinary team.
• Ability to problem solve and self-steer, work to deadlines as necessary, sometimes at short notice.
• Ability to communicate, both in writing and verbally, with audiences of differing technical backgrounds and seniority.
• The ability to work office-based in central London.
It would be nice if you had:
• Although not essential, an appreciation of and interest in aerospace technologies.
• Experience of Python and C# would be a distinct advantage.
What you will get: ·
• Impact: You will help ensure that MOD’s weapon assessments are robust and delivered in a timely manner to UK Defence partners and front-line forces.
• Opportunity: You will play a key role in MOD weapon assessment which is a critical input to MOD’s equipment procurement programs.
• Knowledge: You will develop an understanding of weapon systems and how they operate.
• Skills: You will develop a range of analytical, software and interpersonal skills.
• Insights: You will get to work within a Leonardo team that is fully integrated with its MOD customer which will provide an excellent opportunity to see up-close how the MOD operates.
• Teamwork: You will work with a diverse technical team in a highly collaborative environment.
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.
Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

Guide teams on the design and effective use of semantic data models, including their application to agentic AI solutions

Design and maintain semantic models to support agentic-AI capabilities
